```{julia}
using ForwardDiff   # explicit gradients for Optim (autodiff kwarg pipeline broken in current Optim)

# PrettyTables v3 compatibility shim. v3 dropped `ft_printf` (now
# `fmt__printf`) and requires the `formatters` keyword to be a Vector.
# All call sites in this document use the v2 form
# `formatters = PrettyTables.ft_printf(fmt, cols)`; re-create
# `ft_printf` so it returns a single-element Vector wrapping the new
# `fmt__printf`, accepting either an Int column index or a range.
if !isdefined(PrettyTables, :ft_printf)
    @eval PrettyTables begin
        ft_printf(fmt, cols) =
            [fmt__printf(fmt, collect(cols isa Integer ? (cols:cols) : cols))]
        ft_printf(fmt) = [fmt__printf(fmt)]   # apply to all columns (v2 single-arg)
    end
end

# PrettyTables v3 also renamed the `header` keyword to `column_labels`
# (which must be an `AbstractVector` — a flat vector for one header row,
# or a vector of row-vectors for stacked headers; a Tuple is rejected).
# `_pt_compat` wraps `pretty_table` so the document's v2-style calls keep
# working: it maps `header` → `column_labels` (Tuple → Vector), and
# normalises `formatters` to a flat Vector. All `PrettyTables.pretty_table`
# call sites in the document route through this wrapper. `_PT_REAL` holds
# the real function (no trailing `(`, so the route-through rewrite leaves
# it untouched — no recursion).
const _PT_REAL = PrettyTables.pretty_table
function _pt_compat(data; header = nothing, formatters = nothing,
                    body_hlines = nothing, kwargs...)
    kw = Dict{Symbol,Any}(kwargs)
    if header !== nothing
        kw[:column_labels] = header isa Tuple ? collect(header) : header
    end
    if formatters !== nothing
        kw[:formatters] =
            formatters isa Function ? [formatters] :
            formatters isa Tuple ?
                collect(Iterators.flatten(
                    x isa Union{AbstractVector,Tuple} ? x : (x,) for x in formatters)) :
                formatters
    end
    # `body_hlines` (v2) has no v3 equivalent — it only drew cosmetic
    # horizontal rules after given rows. Captured here and dropped so the
    # table still renders (without the extra separators). `alignment` and
    # `row_labels` are unchanged in v3 and pass straight through.
    return _PT_REAL(data; kw...)
end

# Optim autodiff compat shim. The installed Optim's `autodiff` kwarg
# rejects the Symbol form `:forward` (it now expects an ADTypes type),
# and even the ADTypes path trips a DifferentiationInterface bug in
# this version. The fix: don't use Optim's autodiff plumbing at all —
# wrap `f` with an explicit ForwardDiff-computed gradient and call the
# 5-arg `optimize(f, g!, x0, method, opts)` form, which doesn't go
# through autodiff. `_optimize_compat` routes every Optim.optimize call
# in the document through this translation; 4-arg calls with
# `autodiff = :forward` are rewritten to the 5-arg gradient form, all
# other shapes pass through. `_OPT_REAL` holds the real function (no
# trailing `(`, so the route-through rewrite leaves it untouched).
const _OPT_REAL = Optim.optimize
function _optimize_compat(args...; kwargs...)
    kw = Dict{Symbol,Any}(kwargs)
    ad = pop!(kw, :autodiff, nothing)
    # If `autodiff = :forward` is requested, build the gradient via
    # ForwardDiff and use the explicit-gradient path. Handles any arg
    # shape where args[1]=f, args[2]=x0 (method/options follow): 3-arg
    # `(f, x0, method)`, 4-arg `(f, x0, method, opts)`, etc.
    if ad isa Symbol && (ad === :forward || ad === :forwarddiff) && length(args) >= 2
        f, x0 = args[1], args[2]
        g!(g, x) = ForwardDiff.gradient!(g, f, x)
        return _OPT_REAL(f, g!, x0, args[3:end]...; kw...)
    end
    return ad === nothing ? _OPT_REAL(args...; kw...) :
                            _OPT_REAL(args...; autodiff = ad, kw...)
end
```

```{julia}
_rawval(x) = hasproperty(x, :value) ? x.value : x  # unwrap ReadStatTables.LabeledValue

function _numeric_vec(col)
    vals = collect(skipmissing(col))
    isempty(vals) && return Float64[]
    T = Base.nonmissingtype(eltype(col))
    T <: Real && return convert(Vector{Float64}, vals)
    try
        return Float64[Float64(_rawval(v)) for v in vals]
    catch
        return nothing  # non-numeric (strings, etc.)
    end
end

"""
Expand a Stata-style varlist pattern against DataFrame columns. Supports:
  * `t*`, `*t`, `*mpg*`, `t?`   — glob wildcards
  * `price-weight`              — range of columns (inclusive, by column order)
  * exact names, Symbols, vectors, and the literal "_all"
"""
function _expand_varlist(df, vars)
    cols = string.(DataFrames.names(df))
    patterns = vars isa Union{Symbol,AbstractString} ? [string(vars)] :
               vars isa AbstractVector ? [string(v) for v in vars] :
               [string(v) for v in collect(vars)]

    out = String[]
    for p in patterns
        if p == "_all"
            append!(out, cols)
        elseif occursin('*', p) || occursin('?', p)
            rx = Regex("^" * replace(p, "*" => ".*", "?" => ".") * "\$")
            for c in cols
                occursin(rx, c) && push!(out, c)
            end
        elseif occursin('-', p) && !startswith(p, "-") && !(p in cols)
            parts = split(p, '-', limit=2)
            i = findfirst(==(String(parts[1])), cols)
            j = findfirst(==(String(parts[2])), cols)
            (i === nothing || j === nothing) && error("Unknown variable in range '$p'")
            i, j = minmax(i, j)
            append!(out, cols[i:j])
        else
            push!(out, p)
        end
    end

    seen = Set{String}(); uniq = String[]
    for v in out
        v in seen || (push!(seen, v); push!(uniq, v))
    end
    return Symbol.(uniq)
end

"""
    correlate_stata(df, vars=nothing)

Stata-style `correlate <varlist>` — pairwise (listwise-dropmissing)
correlation matrix of the listed variables, printed in Stata's
lower-triangular layout with abbreviated column headers.

  - `vars` can be `nothing` (use all numeric columns) or a Vector/Tuple of
    column names (Symbol/String).
  - Prints `(obs=N)` then a triangular table with 4-decimal correlations.
  - Variable names longer than 8 chars are abbreviated to `XXXXXX~Y` in the
    column headers, mirroring Stata's wrapping.
  - Returns the full symmetric correlation matrix (`Statistics.cor`) so you
    can keep using it programmatically.
"""
function correlate_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, vars=nothing)
    varlist = vars === nothing ? Symbol[] : Symbol.(vars)
    if isempty(varlist)
        for c in DataFrames.names(df)
            elT = nonmissingtype(eltype(df[!, c]))
            elT <: Real && push!(varlist, Symbol(c))
        end
    end
    sub = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, varlist])
    n   = DataFrames.nrow(sub)
    M   = hcat([Float64.(collect(sub[!, v])) for v in varlist]...)
    C   = Statistics.cor(M)

    abbrev(s::AbstractString, w::Int=8) =
        length(s) <= w ? s : (s[1:w-2] * "~" * s[end:end])
    commafmt(num::Integer) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    println()
    Printf.@printf("(obs=%s)\n\n", commafmt(n))
    Printf.@printf("%12s |", "")
    for v in varlist
        Printf.@printf(" %8s", abbrev(string(v)))
    end
    println()
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^(9 * length(varlist)))
    for (i, v) in enumerate(varlist)
        Printf.@printf("%12s |", string(v))
        for j in 1:i
            Printf.@printf(" %8.4f", C[i, j])
        end
        println()
    end
    return C
end

"""
    histogram_discrete_stata(x; xlabel, ylabel="freq", size=(600,400),
                              bins=nothing, title=nothing)

CairoMakie analogue of Stata's `histogram <var>, discrete xtitle("…")`.
Produces a one-panel `Figure` with integer-valued bins centred on each
observed count. Pass `bins = lo:1:hi` to override the auto-range
(useful for keeping multiple subplots on the same x-axis).
"""
function histogram_discrete_stata(x::AbstractVector;
                                   xlabel::AbstractString,
                                   ylabel::AbstractString = "freq",
                                   size::Tuple{Int,Int} = (600, 400),
                                   bins::Union{Nothing,AbstractRange} = nothing,
                                   title::Union{Nothing,AbstractString} = nothing)
    xint = Int.(x)
    rng  = bins === nothing ?
           ((minimum(xint) - 0.5):1:(maximum(xint) + 0.5)) : bins
    fig  = CairoMakie.Figure(; size = size)
    ax   = title === nothing ?
           CairoMakie.Axis(fig[1, 1]; xlabel, ylabel) :
           CairoMakie.Axis(fig[1, 1]; xlabel, ylabel, title)
    CairoMakie.hist!(ax, xint; bins = rng)
    return fig
end

"""
    histogram_grid_stata(panels; title="", ncols=2, bins=nothing,
                         xlabel="x", ylabel="freq", size=(900,700),
                         common=true, discrete=true, nbins=30)

CairoMakie analogue of Stata's `graph combine g1 g2 …, title(…)
[xcommon ycommon]`. `panels` is a vector of `(data, paneltitle)`
pairs; lays them out row-major in an `ncols`-wide grid with a shared
super-title. `common=true` links the axes across panels (Stata's
`xcommon ycommon`).

`discrete=true` (default) is for count data: each series is rounded to
`Int` and a single shared integer-centred `bins` range is used so the
bars align. `discrete=false` is for continuous series (e.g. fitted
means `predict, mu`): no rounding, and `nbins` equal-width bins span
the pooled data range (override with an explicit `bins`).
"""
function histogram_grid_stata(panels::AbstractVector;
                              title::AbstractString = "",
                              ncols::Int = 2,
                              bins::Union{Nothing,AbstractRange} = nothing,
                              xlabel::AbstractString = "x",
                              ylabel::AbstractString = "freq",
                              size::Tuple{Int,Int} = (900, 700),
                              common::Bool = true,
                              discrete::Bool = true,
                              nbins::Int = 30)
    if discrete
        series = [Int.(p[1]) for p in panels]
        rng = bins === nothing ?
              ((minimum(minimum, series) - 0.5):1:(maximum(maximum, series) + 0.5)) :
              bins
    else
        series = [Float64.(p[1]) for p in panels]
        if bins === nothing
            lo = minimum(minimum, series); hi = maximum(maximum, series)
            rng = range(lo, hi; length = nbins + 1)
        else
            rng = bins
        end
    end
    fig  = CairoMakie.Figure(; size = size)
    isempty(title) ||
        CairoMakie.Label(fig[0, 1:ncols], title; fontsize = 16,
                         font = :bold)
    axs = CairoMakie.Axis[]
    for (k, (_, ptitle)) in enumerate(panels)
        row = div(k - 1, ncols) + 1
        col = mod(k - 1, ncols) + 1
        ax  = CairoMakie.Axis(fig[row, col]; xlabel, ylabel, title = ptitle)
        CairoMakie.hist!(ax, series[k]; bins = rng)
        push!(axs, ax)
    end
    common && length(axs) > 1 && CairoMakie.linkaxes!(axs...)
    return fig
end

function summarize_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, vars=nothing; detail::Bool=false)
    if vars === nothing
        varlist = Symbol[]
        for n in DataFrames.names(df)
            _numeric_vec(df[!, n]) === nothing || push!(varlist, Symbol(n))
        end
    else
        varlist = _expand_varlist(df, vars)
    end

    rows = []
    for v in varlist
        xraw = _numeric_vec(df[!, v])
        x = xraw === nothing ? Float64[] : xraw
        n = length(x)
        if n == 0
            push!(rows, (; Variable=string(v), Obs=0, Mean=missing,
                           Std=missing, Min=missing, Max=missing))
            continue
        end
        μ  = Statistics.mean(x)
        σ  = n > 1 ? Statistics.std(x) : missing
        base = (; Variable=string(v), Obs=n, Mean=μ, Std=σ,
                  Min=minimum(x), Max=maximum(x))
        if detail
            qs = Statistics.quantile(x, [0.01,0.05,0.10,0.25,0.50,0.75,0.90,0.95,0.99])
            # Stata uses biased moments for skewness/kurtosis
            m2 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^2)
            m3 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^3)
            m4 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^4)
            skew = m2 > 0 ? m3 / m2^(3/2) : missing
            kurt = m2 > 0 ? m4 / m2^2     : missing
            push!(rows, merge(base,
                (; p1=qs[1], p5=qs[2], p10=qs[3], p25=qs[4], p50=qs[5],
                   p75=qs[6], p90=qs[7], p95=qs[8], p99=qs[9],
                   Variance = ismissing(σ) ? missing : σ^2,
                   Skewness = skew, Kurtosis = kurt)))
        else
            push!(rows, base)
        end
    end

    # Stata's `summarize, detail` block — one per requested variable.
    if detail
        _g9d(x; w::Int = 9, mx::Int = 7) = begin
            (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return "."
            sig = mx
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
            while length(s) > w && sig > 1
                sig -= 1; s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
            end
            0 < abs(x) < 1 ? replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.") : s
        end
        _comma_d(n::Integer) = replace(string(n), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")
        for r in rows
            v = r.Variable
            x = _numeric_vec(df[!, Symbol(v)])
            x === nothing && (println("$v: not numeric"); continue)
            n = length(x); ssorted = sort(x)
            small4 = ssorted[1:min(4, n)]
            large4 = ssorted[max(1, n - 3):n]    # ascending; Stata also shows ascending here
            println()
            println(lpad(v, 36))
            println("-"^61)
            println(lpad("Percentiles", 26),  lpad("Smallest", 16))
            pct = [0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99]
            qs  = Statistics.quantile(x, pct)
            sml = [get(small4, i, missing) for i in 1:4]
            lrg = [get(large4, i, missing) for i in 1:4]
            # Row 1: 1% / small[1]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "1%",
                           _g9d(qs[1]), _g9d(sml[1]))
            # Row 2: 5% / small[2]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "5%",
                           _g9d(qs[2]), _g9d(sml[2]))
            # Row 3: 10% / small[3]                Obs <N>
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "10%",
                           _g9d(qs[3]), _g9d(sml[3]),
                           "Obs", _comma_d(n))
            # Row 4: 25% / small[4]                Sum of wgt.
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "25%",
                           _g9d(qs[4]), _g9d(sml[4]),
                           "Sum of wgt.", _comma_d(n))
            println()
            # Row 5: 50% / blank          Mean
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "50%",
                           _g9d(qs[5]), "", "Mean", _g9d(r.Mean))
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n",
                           "", "", "Largest",
                           "Std. dev.", _g9d(r.Std))
            # Row 6: 75% / large[1]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "75%",
                           _g9d(qs[6]), _g9d(lrg[1]))
            println()
            # Row 7: 90% / large[2]                Variance
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "90%",
                           _g9d(qs[7]), _g9d(lrg[2]),
                           "Variance", _g9d(r.Variance))
            # Row 8: 95% / large[3]                Skewness
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "95%",
                           _g9d(qs[8]), _g9d(lrg[3]),
                           "Skewness", _g9d(r.Skewness))
            # Row 9: 99% / large[4]                Kurtosis
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "99%",
                           _g9d(qs[9]), _g9d(lrg[4]),
                           "Kurtosis", _g9d(r.Kurtosis))
        end
        return
    end

    # Stata %9.0g: up to 7 sig figs, capped at 9 chars total (so leading "0."
    # for |x|<1 fits), then leading "0" stripped from |x|<1.
    _g9(x; w::Int=9, mx::Int=7) = begin
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return "."
        sig = mx
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        while length(s) > w && sig > 1
            sig -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 ? replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.") : s
    end
    _comma(num::Integer) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    println("    Variable |        Obs        Mean    Std. dev.       Min        Max")
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^57)
    for r in rows
        Printf.@printf("%12s |  %9s   %9s   %9s  %9s  %9s\n",
                       r.Variable, _comma(r.Obs),
                       _g9(r.Mean), _g9(r.Std),
                       _g9(r.Min),  _g9(r.Max))
    end
end

"""
    tabulate_stata(df, var; keep_missing=false)

One-way `tabulate <var>` à la Stata: sorts by the underlying raw value
(so labeled categoricals come out in label-key order) and prints the
Freq / Percent / Cum table with a trailing Total row. Labeled values
from `ReadStatTables` are displayed by their string label; plain
numerics print as themselves. Missings are dropped by default.
"""
function tabulate_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, var::Symbol;
                        keep_missing::Bool=false)
    col = df[!, var]
    mask = keep_missing ? trues(length(col)) : .!ismissing.(col)
    vals = col[mask]
    isempty(vals) && (println("no observations"); return)

    raws = [ismissing(v) ? missing : _rawval(v) for v in vals]
    function _label(v)
        ismissing(v) && return "."
        if hasproperty(v, :labels) && hasproperty(v, :value)
            return haskey(v.labels, v.value) ? v.labels[v.value] : string(v.value)
        end
        return string(v)
    end
    labs = [_label(v) for v in vals]

    # Unique raw keys in their natural order; missing (if kept) goes last.
    raw_nonmissing = sort(unique(skipmissing(raws)))
    keys_sorted = keep_missing && any(ismissing, raws) ?
                  Any[raw_nonmissing...; missing] : Any[raw_nonmissing...]

    # One canonical label per key.
    label_for = Dict{Any,String}()
    for (r, l) in zip(raws, labs)
        haskey(label_for, r) || (label_for[r] = l)
    end

    freqs = [count(x -> isequal(x, k), raws) for k in keys_sorted]
    total = sum(freqs)
    pcts  = freqs ./ total .* 100
    cums  = cumsum(pcts)

    _comma_int(num::Integer) = replace(string(num), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")

    label_strs = [label_for[k] for k in keys_sorted]
    var_w = max(11, length(string(var)),
                maximum(length, label_strs; init=0), length("Total"))

    # Header
    Printf.@printf("%*s |%11s%12s%12s\n", var_w, string(var),
                   "Freq.", "Percent", "Cum.")
    println("-"^(var_w + 1), "+", "-"^35)
    for i in eachindex(keys_sorted)
        Printf.@printf("%*s |%11s%12s%12s\n",
                       var_w, label_strs[i],
                       _comma_int(freqs[i]),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%.2f", pcts[i]),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%.2f", cums[i]))
    end
    println("-"^(var_w + 1), "+", "-"^35)
    Printf.@printf("%*s |%11s%12s\n", var_w, "Total",
                   _comma_int(total), Printf.@sprintf("%.2f", 100.0))
end

"""
    margins_dydx_at_binary_stata(β, V, c; specs, link=:logit,
        depvar="y", vce_label="OIM", level=0.95, n_obs=nothing,
        at_labels=nothing, noatlegend=false)

Stata-style `margins, dydx(*) at(...)` (MER) for a binary GLM (logit
or probit). Computes marginal effects at the user-specified point
`c` (length-k vector in β order, with intercept slot included), with
delta-method SEs via the analytic Jacobian.

`specs` is a vector of `(name::String, kind::Symbol, col_idx::Int)`:
- `kind = :continuous` → analytic derivative `ME = β_j · μ'(c'β)`
   - logit:  μ'(η) = Λ(1−Λ),    μ''(η) = Λ(1−Λ)(1−2Λ)
   - probit: μ'(η) = φ(η),      μ''(η) = −η · φ(η)
   Jacobian: e_j · μ'(η) + β_j · μ''(η) · c
- `kind = :factor` → discrete change `ME = μ(c | x_j=1) − μ(c | x_j=0)`
   Jacobian: μ'(η_1)·c_1 − μ'(η_0)·c_0  (where c_1/c_0 set x_j to 1/0)

Output mirrors Stata's `Conditional marginal effects` block for MER
(header / `dy/dx wrt:` / optional `At:` block + the variable rows).
Factor rows print as `1.<name>` per Stata's i.<var> labeling.

Returns `(; rows = Vector{NamedTuple}, c)` where each row has
`(name, me, se, z, p, ci_lo, ci_hi)`.
"""
function margins_dydx_at_binary_stata(β::AbstractVector, V::AbstractMatrix,
                                      c::AbstractVector;
                                      specs::AbstractVector,
                                      link::Symbol = :logit,
                                      depvar::AbstractString = "y",
                                      vce_label::AbstractString = "OIM",
                                      level::Float64 = 0.95,
                                      n_obs::Union{Nothing,Int} = nothing,
                                      at_labels::Union{Nothing,AbstractVector} = nothing,
                                      noatlegend::Bool = false,
                                      expression::Union{Nothing,AbstractString} = nothing)
    # Link evaluators: μ(η), μ'(η), μ''(η)
    if link == :logit
        μfn(η)   = 1 / (1 + exp(-η))
        μ1fn(η)  = (Λ = μfn(η); Λ * (1 - Λ))
        μ2fn(η)  = (Λ = μfn(η); Λ * (1 - Λ) * (1 - 2*Λ))
    elseif link == :probit
        μfn(η)   = Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), η)
        μ1fn(η)  = Distributions.pdf(Distributions.Normal(), η)
        μ2fn(η)  = -η * Distributions.pdf(Distributions.Normal(), η)
    else
        error("link=$link not supported (use :logit or :probit)")
    end

    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    rows = NamedTuple[]
    for (name, kind, idx) in specs
        if kind == :continuous
            η  = LinearAlgebra.dot(c, β)
            μ1 = μ1fn(η);  μ2 = μ2fn(η)
            me = β[idx] * μ1
            J  = β[idx] .* μ2 .* c
            J[idx] += μ1
            row_label = name
        elseif kind == :factor
            c1 = copy(c); c1[idx] = 1.0
            c0 = copy(c); c0[idx] = 0.0
            η1 = LinearAlgebra.dot(c1, β); η0 = LinearAlgebra.dot(c0, β)
            me = μfn(η1) - μfn(η0)
            J  = μ1fn(η1) .* c1 .- μ1fn(η0) .* c0
            row_label = "1." * name
        else
            error("kind=$kind not supported (use :continuous or :factor)")
        end
        se = sqrt(LinearAlgebra.dot(J, V * J))
        z  = me / se
        p  = 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z)))
        push!(rows, (name = row_label, me = me, se = se, z = z, p = p,
                     ci_lo = me - crit*se, ci_hi = me + crit*se))
    end

    # Stata `%9.0g` formatter
    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    commafmt(num) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    expr = expression === nothing ? "Pr($depvar), predict()" : expression
    println()
    # Header: "Conditional marginal effects" left-padded; "Number of obs"
    # right-aligned at col 78. Stata's exact widths: title in 57, label
    # "Number of obs" in 13, " = ", value right-aligned in 5 → total 78.
    if n_obs !== nothing
        Printf.@printf("%-57s%-13s = %5s\n",
                       "Conditional marginal effects",
                       "Number of obs", commafmt(n_obs))
    else
        println("Conditional marginal effects")
    end
    println("Model VCE: $vce_label")
    println()
    println("Expression: $expr")
    println("dy/dx wrt:  ", join([r.name for r in rows], " "))
    if !noatlegend && at_labels !== nothing
        for (i, kv) in enumerate(at_labels)
            prefix = i == 1 ? "At  : " : "      "
            Printf.@printf("%s%-12s = %s\n", prefix, string(kv.first),
                           string(kv.second))
        end
    end
    println()
    # Coefficient table: 12 (name) + 2 ( | ) + 11 (dy/dx) + 11 (se) +
    # 9 (z) + 8 (p) + 13 (ci_lo) + 12 (ci_hi) = 78 chars.
    println("-"^78)
    println("             |            Delta-method")
    Printf.@printf("%12s |      dy/dx   std. err.      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                   "", 100*level)
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    for r in rows
        Printf.@printf("%12s |%s%s%9.2f%8.3f%s%s\n",
                       r.name,
                       g9(r.me;    w=11),
                       g9(r.se;    w=11),
                       r.z, r.p,
                       g9(r.ci_lo; w=13),
                       g9(r.ci_hi; w=12))
    end
    println("-"^78)
    # Stata adds this note when any factor variable appears in the dy/dx list.
    if any(s -> s[2] == :factor, specs)
        println("Note: dy/dx for factor levels is the discrete change from the base level.")
    end
    return (; rows, c)
end

"""
    margins_dydx_stata(β, V, X; factors, continuous,
                       atmean=false, at=nothing, at_labels=nothing,
                       noatlegend=false,
                       level=0.95, vce_label="Robust",
                       expression="Predicted number of events, predict()")

Unified Stata-style `margins, dydx(*)` — three modes via keyword args:

  - default (`atmean=false, at=nothing`) → **AME** (Stata: `margins, dydx(*)`).
    Title: "Average marginal effects". For each obs, compute ∂ŷ_i/∂x_j or the
    discrete change, then average over the sample.
  - `atmean=true` → **MEM** (Stata: `margins, dydx(*) atmean`). Title:
    "Conditional marginal effects". Evaluated at the sample-mean vector x̄.
  - `at=c` (length-k vector) → **MER** (Stata: `margins, dydx(*) at(...)`).
    Title: "Conditional marginal effects". Evaluated at the user-specified
    point c. Pass `at_labels = [:var=>v, ...]` for the "At:" block, or set
    `noatlegend=true` to suppress it (mirrors Stata's `noatlegend` option).

For each variable:
  - **Factor** (binary 0/1): discrete change ME = μ(x with j=1) − μ(x with j=0).
    Gradient: μ_1·x_1 − μ_0·x_0. For AME, this is averaged across observations.
  - **Continuous**: ME = β_j · μ(x). Gradient: e_j · μ + β_j · μ · x.

`factors` and `continuous` are vectors of `(name, col_idx::Int)` tuples giving
the variable name (no "1." prefix) and its column index in X.
"""
function margins_dydx_stata(β::AbstractVector, V::AbstractMatrix,
                            X::AbstractMatrix;
                            factors::AbstractVector,
                            continuous::AbstractVector,
                            kind::Symbol=:dydx,
                            atmean::Bool=false,
                            at::Union{Nothing,AbstractVector}=nothing,
                            at_labels::Union{Nothing,AbstractVector}=nothing,
                            noatlegend::Bool=false,
                            interactions::AbstractVector=NamedTuple[],
                            level::Float64=0.95,
                            vce_label::String="Robust",
                            expression::String="Predicted number of events, predict()")
    # `interactions` lets the helper handle product interaction columns
    # correctly. Each entry is a NamedTuple `(col=k, base=[i, j, ...])`
    # meaning column k of X is the elementwise product of columns
    # `base`. When a factor variable in `base` flips 0↔1 the helper
    # rebuilds col k from the (possibly modified) base columns; for a
    # continuous variable in `base`, the chain rule for ∂μ/∂x_j picks
    # up an extra `β_k · prod(other base cols)` term.
    # `kind` selects the column header AND the formula for *continuous*
    # variables (factor variables always use the discrete change, since
    # ey/ex of a 0/1 dummy is ill-defined). For Poisson with log link:
    #   :dydx → β_j · μ          (gradient e_j·μ + β_j·μ·x)
    #   :eyex → β_j · x_j        (gradient e_j·x_j;  ε doesn't depend on μ)
    #   :eydx → β_j              (gradient e_j;     semi-elasticity)
    #   :dyex → β_j · μ · x_j    (gradient depends on μ)
    kind in (:dydx, :eyex, :eydx, :dyex) ||
        error("kind must be :dydx, :eyex, :eydx, or :dyex; got $kind")
    kind_label = kind == :dydx ? "dy/dx" :
                 kind == :eyex ? "ey/ex" :
                 kind == :eydx ? "ey/dx" : "dy/ex"
    n, k = size(X)

    g9 = function(x; w_::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w_)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        # Stata's %9.0g effective rule: cap pre-strip at 9 chars EXCEPT for
        # negative |x|<1 where cap=10 (the strip will save 1 char). Without
        # this, negative |x|<1 values lose a digit vs Stata's output.
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w_)
    end
    g_atval = function(x; sig::Int=7)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        # Stata's %9.0g effective rule: cap pre-strip at 9 chars EXCEPT for
        # negative |x|<1 where cap=10 (the strip will save 1 char). Without
        # this, negative |x|<1 values lose a digit vs Stata's output.
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        s
    end
    commafmt(num::Integer) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    _summary(dydx, se) = begin
        z = dydx / se
        p = 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z)))
        (z, p, dydx - crit*se, dydx + crit*se)
    end

    # Determine evaluation mode
    if at !== nothing
        mode  = :atpoint
        x_eval = collect(at)
        length(x_eval) == k ||
            error("at must have length(β)=$k, got $(length(x_eval))")
    elseif atmean
        mode  = :atmean
        x_eval = vec(Statistics.mean(X, dims = 1))
    else
        mode  = :average
        x_eval = nothing
    end

    title = mode == :average ? "Average marginal effects" :
                               "Conditional marginal effects"

    # _refresh_interactions! rebuilds any interaction column whose `base`
    # includes `idx` from the (possibly mutated) base columns. Used when
    # flipping a factor between 0 and 1 in the AME / atmean / atpoint path.
    function _refresh_interactions!(Xm::AbstractMatrix, idx::Integer)
        for intr in interactions
            if idx in intr.base
                col = ones(size(Xm, 1))
                for b in intr.base
                    col .*= Xm[:, b]
                end
                Xm[:, intr.col] .= col
            end
        end
    end
    function _refresh_interactions_vec!(xv::AbstractVector, idx::Integer)
        for intr in interactions
            if idx in intr.base
                v = 1.0
                for b in intr.base
                    v *= xv[b]
                end
                xv[intr.col] = v
            end
        end
    end

    # Compute each variable's dy/dx and its delta-method SE
    rows = Tuple[]
    for (nm, idx) in factors
        if mode == :average
            X0 = copy(X); X0[:, idx] .= 0.0; _refresh_interactions!(X0, idx)
            X1 = copy(X); X1[:, idx] .= 1.0; _refresh_interactions!(X1, idx)
            μ0 = exp.(X0 * β); μ1 = exp.(X1 * β)
            dydx = Statistics.mean(μ1 .- μ0)
            gvec = vec((μ1' * X1 .- μ0' * X0) ./ n)
        else
            x0 = copy(x_eval); x0[idx] = 0.0; _refresh_interactions_vec!(x0, idx)
            x1 = copy(x_eval); x1[idx] = 1.0; _refresh_interactions_vec!(x1, idx)
            μ0 = exp(LinearAlgebra.dot(x0, β))
            μ1 = exp(LinearAlgebra.dot(x1, β))
            dydx = μ1 - μ0
            gvec = μ1 .* x1 .- μ0 .* x0
        end
        se = sqrt(gvec' * V * gvec)
        push!(rows, ("1.$nm", dydx, se, _summary(dydx, se)...))
    end
    # Interactions involving variable `idx` — used by :dydx for both the AME
    # slope and its gradient (chain rule picks up β_intr · prod_other terms).
    function _intr_extras(idx::Integer, X_::AbstractMatrix)
        out = NamedTuple[]
        for intr in interactions
            if idx in intr.base
                po = ones(size(X_, 1))
                for b in intr.base
                    b == idx && continue
                    po .*= X_[:, b]
                end
                push!(out, (col = intr.col, prod_other = po))
            end
        end
        out
    end
    function _intr_extras_vec(idx::Integer, xv::AbstractVector)
        out = NamedTuple[]
        for intr in interactions
            if idx in intr.base
                v = 1.0
                for b in intr.base
                    b == idx && continue
                    v *= xv[b]
                end
                push!(out, (col = intr.col, prod_other_at = v))
            end
        end
        out
    end

    for (nm, idx) in continuous
        if mode == :average
            μ_all = exp.(X * β)
            μ̄    = Statistics.mean(μ_all)
            x̄_j  = Statistics.mean(X[:, idx])
            if kind == :dydx
                # ∂μ_i/∂x_j = μ_i · slope_i where slope_i = β_j + Σ β_intr · prod_other
                xtras = _intr_extras(idx, X)
                slope = fill(β[idx], n)
                for x in xtras
                    slope .+= β[x.col] .* x.prod_other
                end
                dydx = Statistics.mean(μ_all .* slope)
                gvec = vec((μ_all .* slope)' * X) ./ n
                gvec[idx] += sum(μ_all) / n
                for x in xtras
                    gvec[x.col] += sum(μ_all .* x.prod_other) / n
                end
            elseif kind == :eyex
                # ey/ex averaged over the sample = β_j · mean(x_j)  (Poisson log)
                dydx = β[idx] * x̄_j
                gvec = zeros(k); gvec[idx] = x̄_j
            elseif kind == :eydx
                dydx = β[idx]
                gvec = zeros(k); gvec[idx] = 1.0
            else  # :dyex — dy/d(ln x) = β_j · μ · x_j
                dydx = β[idx] * μ̄ * x̄_j
                gvec = zeros(k); gvec[idx] = μ̄ * x̄_j
                gvec .+= β[idx] * x̄_j .* vec((μ_all' * X) ./ n)
            end
        else
            μ_at = exp(LinearAlgebra.dot(x_eval, β))
            xj   = x_eval[idx]
            if kind == :dydx
                # slope_at = β_j + Σ β_intr · prod_other (eval at point)
                xtras = _intr_extras_vec(idx, x_eval)
                slope_at = β[idx]
                for x in xtras
                    slope_at += β[x.col] * x.prod_other_at
                end
                dydx = μ_at * slope_at
                gvec = μ_at * slope_at .* x_eval
                gvec[idx] += μ_at
                for x in xtras
                    gvec[x.col] += μ_at * x.prod_other_at
                end
            elseif kind == :eyex
                # ey/ex at the eval point = β_j · x_j  (Poisson log link makes
                # this independent of μ — gradient picks up only the β_j slot)
                dydx = β[idx] * xj
                gvec = zeros(k); gvec[idx] = xj
            elseif kind == :eydx
                dydx = β[idx]
                gvec = zeros(k); gvec[idx] = 1.0
            else  # :dyex
                dydx = β[idx] * μ_at * xj
                gvec = zeros(k); gvec[idx] = μ_at * xj
                gvec .+= β[idx] * μ_at * xj .* x_eval
            end
        end
        se = sqrt(gvec' * V * gvec)
        push!(rows, (string(nm), dydx, se, _summary(dydx, se)...))
    end

    dydx_names = vcat(["1.$nm" for (nm, _) in factors],
                      [string(nm) for (nm, _) in continuous])

    println()
    Printf.@printf("%-57s%-13s = %5s\n",
                   title, "Number of obs", commafmt(n))
    Printf.@printf("Model VCE: %s\n", vce_label)
    println()
    Printf.@printf("Expression: %s\n", expression)
    Printf.@printf("%s wrt:  %s\n", kind_label, join(dydx_names, " "))

    # "At:" block (only for atmean / atpoint, and only if not suppressed)
    if !noatlegend && mode != :average
        if mode == :atmean
            at_lines = Tuple[]
            for (nm, idx) in factors
                m1 = Statistics.mean(X[:, idx])
                push!(at_lines, ("0.$nm", 1.0 - m1))
                push!(at_lines, ("1.$nm", m1))
            end
            for (nm, idx) in continuous
                push!(at_lines, (string(nm), x_eval[idx]))
            end
            max_name_w = maximum(length(t[1]) for t in at_lines)
            for (i, (nm, val)) in enumerate(at_lines)
                prefix = i == 1 ? "At: " : "    "
                Printf.@printf("%s%-*s = %s (mean)\n",
                               prefix, max_name_w, nm, g_atval(val))
            end
        elseif at_labels !== nothing && !isempty(at_labels)
            max_name_w = maximum(length(string(p_.first)) for p_ in at_labels)
            val_strs   = [Printf.@sprintf("%g", float(p_.second)) for p_ in at_labels]
            max_val_w  = maximum(length, val_strs)
            for (i, p_) in enumerate(at_labels)
                prefix = i == 1 ? "At: " : "    "
                Printf.@printf("%s%-*s = %s\n",
                               prefix, max_name_w, string(p_.first),
                               lpad(val_strs[i], max_val_w))
            end
        end
    end

    println()
    println("-"^78)
    println("             |            Delta-method")
    Printf.@printf("             |      %s   std. err.      z    P>|z|     [95%% conf. interval]\n", kind_label)
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    for (lab, dydx, se, z, p, lo, hi) in rows
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                       lab, g9(dydx; w_=10), g9(se; w_=9),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p),
                       g9(lo; w_=9), g9(hi; w_=10))
    end
    println("-"^78)
    !isempty(factors) && println("Note: dy/dx for factor levels is the discrete change from the base level.")
    return rows
end

"""
    regress_stata(model; level=0.95)

Stata-style `regress` output — prints the ANOVA table, overall F-statistic,
R², adjusted R², Root MSE, and the coefficient table with t-statistics,
p-values, and confidence intervals, matching the format of Stata's
`regress` command. The intercept is relabelled `_cons`.

Works with any `StatsBase`-compatible OLS model, e.g. the output of
`FixedEffectModels.reg(df, @formula(y ~ x2 + x3))`.
"""
function regress_stata(model; level::Float64=0.95, noheader::Bool=false)
    β      = StatsBase.coef(model)
    V      = StatsBase.vcov(model)
    se     = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    nm_raw = string.(StatsBase.coefnames(model))
    nm     = replace.(nm_raw, "(Intercept)" => "_cons")
    has_int = any(==("_cons"), nm)

    n      = Int(StatsBase.nobs(model))
    rss    = StatsBase.deviance(model)
    r2     = StatsBase.r2(model)
    ar2    = StatsBase.adjr2(model)
    dof_r  = Int(StatsBase.dof_residual(model))
    k      = length(β) - (has_int ? 1 : 0)
    tss    = rss / max(1 - r2, eps())
    mss    = tss - rss
    rmse   = sqrt(rss / dof_r)
    Fstat  = (mss / k) / (rss / dof_r)
    pF     = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.FDist(k, dof_r), Fstat)

    yname = try
        string(StatsBase.responsename(model))
    catch
        hasproperty(model, :yname) ? string(model.yname) : "y"
    end

    t_stat = β ./ se
    tcrit  = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.TDist(dof_r), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    p_val  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.TDist(dof_r), abs.(t_stat)))
    ci_lo  = β .- tcrit .* se
    ci_hi  = β .+ tcrit .* se

    # Stata %10.0g-style: `sig` significant digits, strip leading 0 for |x|<1,
    # right-aligned in width `w`.
    function _g(x, w; sig=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return Printf.@sprintf("%*s", w, ".")
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        if 0 < abs(x) < 1
            s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.")
        end
        return Printf.@sprintf("%*s", w, s)
    end

    # ── ANOVA table + summary-stats block (skipped when `noheader=true`,
    # matching Stata's `regress y x, noheader` option)
    if !noheader
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %10s %10s %10s    %-13s = %10d\n",
                       "Source", "SS", "df", "MS", "Number of obs", n)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^34, "   ",
                Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %10.2f", "F($k, $dof_r)", Fstat))
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s %10d %s    %-13s = %10.4f\n",
                       "Model", _g(mss, 10), k, _g(mss/k, 10), "Prob > F", pF)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s %10d %s    %-13s = %10.4f\n",
                       "Residual", _g(rss, 10), dof_r, _g(rss/dof_r, 10),
                       "R-squared", r2)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^34, "   ",
                Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %10.4f", "Adj R-squared", ar2))
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s %10d %s    %-13s = %10.4f\n",
                       "Total", _g(tss, 10), n-1, _g(tss/(n-1), 10),
                       "Root MSE", rmse)
    end
    println()

    # ── Coefficient table
    println("-"^78)
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %10s  %9s  %6s  %5s     [%d%% conf. interval]\n",
                   yname, "Coefficient", "Std. err.", "t", "P>|t|",
                   round(Int, 100*level))
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    for i in eachindex(β)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %6.2f  %5.3f  %s  %s\n",
                       nm[i],
                       _g(β[i], 10),
                       _g(se[i], 9),
                       t_stat[i],
                       p_val[i],
                       _g(ci_lo[i], 11),
                       _g(ci_hi[i], 11))
    end
    println("-"^78)
    return nothing
end

"""
    regress_stata(df, y, xs; level=0.95, vcov=nothing)

Convenience method: fit `y ~ xs…` on `df` with `FixedEffectModels.reg` and
print the Stata-style `regress` output. `y` is the dependent variable (Symbol
or String); `xs` is a Symbol, String, or vector of regressor names. Pass
`vcov=Vcov.robust()` (or similar) for non-default standard errors.

Example:

    regress_stata(df5, :y, [:x2, :x3])
    regress_stata(df5, :y, [:x2, :x3]; vcov=Vcov.robust())
"""
function regress_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, y, xs;
                       level::Float64=0.95, vcov=nothing, weights=nothing,
                       noheader::Bool=false)
    ys  = Symbol(y)
    xsv = xs isa Union{Symbol,AbstractString} ? [Symbol(xs)] :
          [Symbol(v) for v in xs]
    f = term(ys) ~ sum(term.(xsv))
    kw = weights === nothing ? (;) : (; weights=Symbol(weights))
    m = vcov === nothing ?
        FixedEffectModels.reg(df, f; kw...) :
        FixedEffectModels.reg(df, f, vcov; kw...)
    regress_stata(m; level=level, noheader=noheader)
    return nothing
end

"""
    nl_exp_stata(df, depvar, regs; vce=:robust, level=0.95, quiet=false,
                 β0=nothing) -> NamedTuple

Stata's `nl (y = exp({xb: <regs> _cons})), vce(robust|oim)` — nonlinear
least squares with exponential mean function:

    y_i = exp(x_i'β) + u_i,    minimise Σ(y_i − exp(x_i'β))²

For Poisson-like count data this is the "NLS-Poisson" estimator, identical
to Poisson MLE only when the conditional mean is correctly specified but
without exploiting the Poisson variance structure. SEs default to the
Huber–White sandwich (analogous to Stata's `vce(robust)`):

    V = (G'G)⁻¹ · G'·diag((y − μ̂)²)·G · (G'G)⁻¹ · n/(n − k)

with G_i = μ̂_i · x_i (Jacobian of the mean function).

Prints the Stata-style "Nonlinear regression" block (Number of obs, R²,
Root MSE) plus the coefficient table, with "/xb_<regname>" parameter
labels matching Stata's `{xb: …}` notation.

Returns `(; β, V, se, μ̂, residuals, ll, RSS, R2, RMSE, n, k, coefnames)`.
"""
function nl_exp_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, depvar::Symbol,
                     regs::AbstractVector{Symbol};
                     vce::Symbol = :robust, level::Float64 = 0.95,
                     quiet::Bool = false,
                     β0::Union{Nothing, AbstractVector} = nothing)
    cols = vcat([depvar], collect(regs))
    dfc  = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, cols])
    for c in cols
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing,Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(_rawval.(col))
        end
    end
    y  = Float64.(_rawval.(dfc[!, depvar]))
    Xm = hcat([Float64.(_rawval.(dfc[!, r])) for r in regs]..., ones(length(y)))
    n  = length(y); k = size(Xm, 2)
    coefnames = vcat(string.(regs), "_cons")

    obj(β) = sum((y .- exp.(Xm * β)).^2)
    β_start = β0 === nothing ?
              vcat(zeros(k - 1), log(max(Statistics.mean(y), eps()))) :
              collect(β0)
    res = _optimize_compat(obj, β_start, Optim.LBFGS(),
                         Optim.Options(g_tol = 1e-8, iterations = 500);
                         autodiff = :forward)
    β̂  = Optim.minimizer(res)
    μ̂  = exp.(Xm * β̂)
    e  = y .- μ̂
    RSS = sum(e.^2)
    σ̂² = RSS / (n - k)
    RMSE = sqrt(σ̂²)
    TSS = sum((y .- Statistics.mean(y)).^2)
    R2  = 1 - RSS / TSS

    # Jacobian rows: ∂μ_i/∂β = μ_i · x_i
    G = μ̂ .* Xm
    GtG = G' * G
    GtG_inv = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.cholesky(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(GtG)))
    if vce == :robust
        meat = G' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(e.^2) * G
        V = GtG_inv * meat * GtG_inv * (n / (n - k))
        vce_label = "Robust"
    else
        V = GtG_inv * σ̂²
        vce_label = "OIM"
    end
    se = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    z  = β̂ ./ se
    p  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    ll  = -n/2 * log(2 * Base.pi * σ̂²) - n/2

    function g9(x; w::Int = 10, sig::Int = 7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        su = sig; s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", su, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && su > 1
            su -= 1; s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", su, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    commafmt(num) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    if !quiet
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%-50s%-13s = %10s\n",
                       "Nonlinear regression",
                       "Number of obs", commafmt(n))
        Printf.@printf("%50s%-13s = %10.4f\n", "", "R-squared", R2)
        Printf.@printf("%50s%-13s = %10.4f\n", "", "Root MSE", RMSE)
        Printf.@printf("%50s%-13s = %10.4f\n", "", "Res. dev.",
                       n * log(RSS / n))
        println()
        println("-"^78)
        if vce == :robust
            println("             |               Robust")
        end
        se_label = vce == :robust ? "std. err." : "Std. err."
        Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  %s      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       string(depvar), se_label, 100 * level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        for i in 1:k
            lab = coefnames[i] == "_cons" ? "/xb_one" : "/xb_$(coefnames[i])"
            lo = β̂[i] - crit * se[i]; hi = β̂[i] + crit * se[i]
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           lab, g9(β̂[i]; w=10), g9(se[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p[i]),
                           g9(lo; w=9), g9(hi; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^78)
    end

    return (; β = β̂, V, se, μ̂, residuals = e,
              ll, RSS, R2, RMSE, n, k, coefnames, vce_label)
end

"""
    correlate(df, vars; filter_missing=Symbol[])

Stata-style `correlate varlist [if …]` — prints the lower-triangular
Pearson correlation matrix with 4-decimal display and Stata's 8-char
variable-name truncation via `~`. Pass extra variables in
`filter_missing` to emulate Stata's `if var != .` subsetting (rows with
missing on any listed variable are dropped in addition to the `vars`
themselves).

Returns the `n × n` correlation matrix.
"""
function correlate(df, vars::AbstractVector; filter_missing=Symbol[])
    vars_v   = [Symbol(v) for v in vars]
    filter_v = [Symbol(v) for v in filter_missing]
    d        = DataFrames.dropmissing(df, unique(vcat(vars_v, filter_v)))
    M        = hcat([Float64.(_rawval.(d[!, v])) for v in vars_v]...)
    R        = Statistics.cor(M)
    n_var    = length(vars_v)

    _trunc(s) = length(s) <= 8 ? s : s[1:6] * "~" * s[end:end]
    nms       = string.(vars_v)
    nms_disp  = _trunc.(nms)

    hdr = Printf.@sprintf("%12s |", "")
    for nm in nms_disp
        hdr *= Printf.@sprintf(" %8s", nm)
    end
    println(hdr)
    println("-"^13 * "+" * "-"^(9 * n_var))

    for i in 1:n_var
        row = Printf.@sprintf("%12s |", nms[i])
        for j in 1:i
            row *= Printf.@sprintf("%9.4f", R[i, j])
        end
        println(row)
    end
    return R
end

"""
    correlate(df, vars)

Stata-style `correlate var1 var2 ...`. Prints a lower-triangular correlation
matrix on pairwise-complete rows, with row labels like Stata.
"""
function correlate(df, vars::AbstractVector)
    m = Matrix{Float64}(undef, DataFrames.nrow(df), length(vars))
    for (j, v) in enumerate(vars)
        m[:, j] = [ismissing(x) ? NaN : Float64(_rawval(x)) for x in df[!, Symbol(v)]]
    end
    keep = .!any(isnan, m; dims=2)[:]
    m = m[keep, :]
    n = size(m, 1)
    C = Statistics.cor(m)
    disp = [i < j ? "" : Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", C[i, j])
            for i in 1:length(vars), j in 1:length(vars)]
    println("(obs = $n)")
    out = DataFrames.DataFrame()
    out[!, :Variable] = string.(vars)
    for (j, v) in enumerate(vars)
        out[!, Symbol(v)] = disp[:, j]
    end
    _pt_compat(out; alignment=:r)
    return (; cor=C, n=n, vars=string.(vars))
end

"""
    boot_regtable(β, β_boot; coefnames, title="", level=0.95)

Stata-style regression table from a point estimate `β` and a `B × k` matrix of
bootstrap replicates `β_boot`. Reports Coef / Bootstrap SE / z / P>|z| / CI
exactly like Stata prints after `vce(boot)`.
"""
function boot_regtable(β::AbstractVector, β_boot::AbstractMatrix;
                       coefnames, title::String = "", level::Float64 = 0.95)
    se   = Statistics.std(β_boot, dims=1)[:]
    z    = β ./ se
    pval = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    lo   = β .- crit .* se
    hi   = β .+ crit .* se
    isempty(title) || println(title)
    Printf.@printf("  (bootstrap replications = %d)\n\n", size(β_boot, 1))
    _pt_compat(
        DataFrames.DataFrame(
            variable   = string.(coefnames),
            estimate   = β,
            boot_se    = se,
            z          = z,
            p          = pval,
            ci_lo      = lo,
            ci_hi      = hi);
        formatters = PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.6f", 2:7))
    return (; β, se, z, p=pval, ci_lo=lo, ci_hi=hi)
end

"""
    boot_table_stata(β, β_boot; coefnames, n, level=0.95, depvar="")

Stata's `Bootstrap results` block (e.g. after `bootstrap _b, reps(B)`).
`β` is the observed (full-sample) point estimate, `β_boot` a `B × k`
matrix of replicates; `coefnames` and `β` are assumed already in
display order (slopes first, `_cons` last). Prints

    Observed coefficient | Bootstrap std. err. | z | P>|z| |
    Normal-based [conf. interval]

with Stata's %9.0g number formatting. Bootstrap SE = sd of the
replicates; CIs are the normal-based β ± z·SE. Returns `(; se, z, p)`.
"""
function boot_table_stata(β::AbstractVector, β_boot::AbstractMatrix;
                          coefnames, n::Integer, level::Float64 = 0.95)
    se   = vec(Statistics.std(β_boot, dims = 1))
    z    = β ./ se
    p    = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    B    = size(β_boot, 1)

    function g9(x; w::Int = 10, sig::Int = 7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        su = sig; s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", su, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && su > 1
            su -= 1; s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", su, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    commafmt(num::Integer) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    nstr = commafmt(n); bstr = commafmt(B)
    vw   = max(length(nstr), length(bstr))      # value field = widest value
    println()
    Printf.@printf("%-57s%-13s = %*s\n", "Bootstrap results",
                   "Number of obs", vw, nstr)
    Printf.@printf("%57s%-13s = %*s\n", "", "Replications", vw, bstr)
    println()
    println("-"^78)
    println("             |   Observed   Bootstrap                         Normal-based")
    Printf.@printf("%12s | coefficient  std. err.      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                   "", 100*level)
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    for i in eachindex(β)
        lo = β[i] - crit*se[i]; hi = β[i] + crit*se[i]
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                       string(coefnames[i]), g9(β[i]; w=10), g9(se[i]; w=9),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z[i]),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p[i]),
                       g9(lo; w=9), g9(hi; w=10))
    end
    println("-"^78)
    return (; se, z, p)
end

"""
    obs_bootstrap(f, df; B=400, seed=10101, verbose=true)

Observation-level bootstrap — resamples n rows with replacement (no cluster
structure). Matches Stata's `vce(bootstrap)` when no cluster is specified.
"""
function obs_bootstrap(f::Function, df; B::Int=400, seed::Int=10101, verbose::Bool=true)
    rng = Random.MersenneTwister(seed)
    n = nrow(df)
    results = Vector{Vector{Float64}}()
    n_fail = 0
    for b in 1:B
        row_idx = StatsBase.sample(rng, 1:n, n; replace=true)
        sub = df[row_idx, :]
        try
            push!(results, f(sub))
        catch
            n_fail += 1
        end
    end
    verbose && n_fail > 0 && @warn "Bootstrap: $n_fail/$B resamples failed."
    isempty(results) && error("All bootstrap resamples failed.")
    return reduce(hcat, results)'
end

"""
    boot_cf_poisson_stata(df; count_dep, endog, exog, instruments,
                          B=400, seed=10101, level=0.95, title="") -> NamedTuple

Bootstrap of the control-function two-step Poisson estimator — the Julia
counterpart of Stata's `program endogtwostep … ; bootstrap _b, reps()
seed()`. Each replicate (and the point estimate):

  1. OLS first stage: `endog ~ exog + instruments`; residual = control fn.
  2. Poisson second stage: `count_dep ~ endog + exog + residual`.

Resampling the whole two-step propagates first-stage estimation
uncertainty into the SEs (the naive robust SEs on the single second-stage
fit omit it). Uses chunk-1 `obs_bootstrap` (observation resampling) and
prints via `boot_regtable`. Returns `(; β, β_boot, coefnames)`.
"""
function boot_cf_poisson_stata(df; count_dep::Symbol, endog::Symbol,
                               exog::AbstractVector{Symbol},
                               instruments::AbstractVector{Symbol},
                               B::Int = 400, seed::Int = 10101,
                               level::Float64 = 0.95, title::String = "",
                               resid_label::AbstractString = "lpuhat2")
    cols = unique(vcat([count_dep, endog], collect(exog), collect(instruments)))
    dfc  = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, cols])
    resid_sym = :_cf_resid_
    fml1 = StatsModels.term(endog) ~
           sum(StatsModels.term.(vcat(collect(exog), collect(instruments))))
    fml2 = StatsModels.term(count_dep) ~
           sum(StatsModels.term.(vcat([endog], collect(exog), [resid_sym])))

    function _step(sub)
        m1 = FixedEffectModels.reg(sub, fml1)
        s2 = DataFrames.copy(sub)
        s2[!, resid_sym] = s2[!, endog] .- FixedEffectModels.predict(m1, s2)
        m2 = GLM.glm(fml2, s2, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink())
        return GLM.coef(m2)
    end

    # Point estimate + coefnames from the full sample.
    s0 = DataFrames.copy(dfc)
    m1_0 = FixedEffectModels.reg(s0, fml1)
    s0[!, resid_sym] = s0[!, endog] .- FixedEffectModels.predict(m1_0, s0)
    m2_0 = GLM.glm(fml2, s0, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink())
    β  = GLM.coef(m2_0)
    cn_raw = GLM.coefnames(m2_0)
    β_boot = obs_bootstrap(_step, dfc; B = B, seed = seed)

    # Reorder to Stata display order: slopes (formula order) first,
    # `_cons` last; relabel the control-function residual.
    cons_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn_raw)
    slope_idx = setdiff(1:length(β), cons_idx === nothing ? Int[] : [cons_idx])
    ord = vcat(slope_idx, cons_idx === nothing ? Int[] : [cons_idx])
    relabel(c) = c == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" :
                 c == string(resid_sym) ? resid_label : c
    cn = [relabel(cn_raw[i]) for i in ord]

    isempty(title) || println(title)
    boot_table_stata(β[ord], β_boot[:, ord];
                     coefnames = cn, n = DataFrames.nrow(dfc), level = level)
    return (; β = β[ord], β_boot = β_boot[:, ord], coefnames = cn)
end

"""
    poisson_gmm_stata(df, depvar, xvars, zvars; twostep=false, level=0.95,
                      quiet=false) -> NamedTuple

Nonlinear-IV (GMM) Poisson — the Julia counterpart of the textbook's Mata
`pgmm` program. Moment conditions E[Z'(y − exp(Xβ))] = 0 with
   Q(β) = h'W h,   h = Z'(y − μ),   μ = exp(Xβ).
`xvars` are the count regressors (including the endogenous one), `zvars`
the instruments (excluded instruments + exogenous regressors); a constant
is appended to both X and Z. One-step uses W = (Z'Z)⁻¹; `twostep=true`
re-weights by the optimal Ŝ⁻¹ from first-step residuals.

Robust (GMM-sandwich) vcov, matching the Mata code:
   G = −(μ ⊙ Z)'X,  Ŝ = ((y−μ)⊙Z)'((y−μ)⊙Z)·n/(n−k),
   V = (G'WG)⁻¹ G'W Ŝ W G (G'WG)⁻¹.

Prints a Stata-style coefficient table. Returns `(; β, V, se, coefnames,
X, Z, y, n, k, W, df)`.
"""
function poisson_gmm_stata(df, depvar::Symbol,
                           xvars::AbstractVector{Symbol},
                           zvars::AbstractVector{Symbol};
                           twostep::Bool = false, level::Float64 = 0.95,
                           quiet::Bool = false)
    cols = unique(vcat([depvar], collect(xvars), collect(zvars)))
    dfc  = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, cols])
    for c in cols
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing,Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(_rawval.(col))
        end
    end
    y = Float64.(_rawval.(dfc[!, depvar])); n = length(y)
    X = hcat([Float64.(_rawval.(dfc[!, v])) for v in xvars]..., ones(n))
    Z = hcat([Float64.(_rawval.(dfc[!, v])) for v in zvars]..., ones(n))
    k = size(X, 2)
    xnames = vcat(string.(xvars), "_cons")

    Wmat = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.cholesky(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(Z'Z)))
    # Objective Q(β)=h'Wh with analytic gradient ∇Q = 2·G'W·h and the
    # Gauss-Newton Hessian 2·G'WG, where h = Z'(y−μ), μ = exp(Xβ),
    # G = ∂h/∂β = −(μ⊙Z)'X. This is exactly the Mata `pgmm` d2
    # evaluator; Newton's method converges from β = 0 (plain LBFGS
    # stalls on this surface), and it sidesteps the autodiff API.
    Qf(W) = β -> (h = Z' * (y .- exp.(X*β)); h' * W * h)
    Qg!(W) = (g, β) -> begin
        μ = exp.(X*β); h = Z' * (y .- μ); G = -(μ .* Z)' * X
        g .= 2 .* (G' * (W * h)); g
    end
    Qh!(W) = (H, β) -> begin
        μ = exp.(X*β); G = -(μ .* Z)' * X
        H .= 2 .* (G' * W * G); H
    end
    _fit(W, β0) = Optim.minimizer(_optimize_compat(Qf(W), Qg!(W), Qh!(W), β0,
                       Optim.Newton(), Optim.Options(iterations = 1000,
                                                     g_tol = 1e-10)))
    β = _fit(Wmat, zeros(k))
    if twostep
        e1   = y .- exp.(X*β)
        Wmat = LinearAlgebra.inv(((e1 .* Z)' * (e1 .* Z)) / n)
        β    = _fit(Wmat, β)
    end

    μ    = exp.(X*β)
    G    = -(μ .* Z)' * X
    Shat = ((y .- μ) .* Z)' * ((y .- μ) .* Z) * (n / (n - k))
    GWG  = G' * Wmat * G
    GWGi = LinearAlgebra.inv(GWG)
    V    = GWGi * G' * Wmat * Shat * Wmat * G * GWGi
    se   = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    z    = β ./ se
    p    = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)

    if !quiet
        function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
            (ismissing(x)||!isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
            su=sig; s=Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", su, x); cap=(0<abs(x)<1 && x<0) ? 10 : 9
            while length(s)>cap && su>1; su-=1; s=Printf.@sprintf("%.*g",su,x); end
            0<abs(x)<1 && (s=replace(s, r"^(-?)0\."=>s"\1.")); lpad(s,w)
        end
        commafmt(num::Integer)=begin s=string(abs(num)); ps=String[]; i=length(s)
            while i>=1; push!(ps,s[max(1,i-2):i]); i-=3; end; (num<0 ? "-" : "")*join(reverse(ps),",") end
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%-52s%-13s = %8s\n",
                       twostep ? "Poisson GMM (two-step)" : "Poisson GMM (one-step)",
                       "Number of obs", commafmt(n))
        println("-"^78)
        println("             |               Robust")
        Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  std. err.      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       string(depvar), 100*level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        ord = vcat(1:(k-1), [k])    # slopes then _cons
        for i in ord
            lo=β[i]-crit*se[i]; hi=β[i]+crit*se[i]
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           xnames[i], g9(β[i];w=10), g9(se[i];w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p[i]),
                           g9(lo;w=9), g9(hi;w=10))
        end
        println("-"^78)
    end

    # Hansen's J statistic for the test of overidentifying restrictions
    # (`estat overid`). With h = Z'(y−μ̂) = N·ḡ and the two-step optimal
    # weight W = Ŝ⁻¹, J = N·ḡ'Ŝ⁻¹ḡ = (h'Wh)/N ~ χ²(#instruments −
    # #params). Only valid after the *two-step* fit (W = Ŝ⁻¹); for
    # one-step it is reported but not the efficient-GMM J.
    h_final = Z' * (y .- exp.(X*β))
    Jstat = (h_final' * Wmat * h_final) / n
    J_df  = size(Z, 2) - size(X, 2)
    J_p   = J_df > 0 ? 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(J_df), Jstat) : NaN

    return (; β, V, se, coefnames = xnames, X, Z, y, n, k, W = Wmat, df = dfc,
              twostep, Jstat, J_df, J_p)
end

"""
    estat_overid_gmm_stata(gmm_res)

Stata's `estat overid` after `gmm` — Hansen's J test of overidentifying
restrictions, read from a `poisson_gmm_stata(...; twostep=true)` result.
Prints `J = …, chi2(df) = …, Prob > chi2 = …`. (Valid only after the
two-step fit, where the weight matrix is the optimal Ŝ⁻¹.)
"""
function estat_overid_gmm_stata(gmm_res)
    gmm_res.twostep ||
        @warn "estat overid: J is the efficient-GMM statistic only after the two-step fit."
    println()
    Printf.@printf("Test of overidentifying restriction:\n")
    Printf.@printf("Hansen's J chi2(%d) = %.5f  (p = %.4f)\n",
                   gmm_res.J_df, gmm_res.Jstat, gmm_res.J_p)
    return (; J = gmm_res.Jstat, df = gmm_res.J_df, p = gmm_res.J_p)
end

"""
    estimates_stats_stata(models) -> NamedTuple

Stata's `estimates stats <m1> <m2> …` — side-by-side AIC/BIC comparison.
`models` is a vector of tuples `(name, n, ll, df)` or, to fill the
`ll(null)` column (each command's `e(ll_0)`, the intercept-only fit's
log-likelihood), `(name, n, ll, df, ll_null)`. A missing/`NaN` ll_null
prints as ".". Per row:

    AIC = −2·ll + 2·df,   BIC = −2·ll + df·log(N).

Prints Stata's wide table; returns `(; aic, bic)` vectors in input order.
"""
function estimates_stats_stata(models::AbstractVector)
    commafmt(num::Integer) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end
    aics = Float64[]; bics = Float64[]
    println("\nAkaike's information criterion and Bayesian information criterion\n")
    println("-"^78)
    println("       Model |          N   ll(null)  ll(model)      df        AIC        BIC")
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    for row in models
        name, n, ll, df = row[1], row[2], row[3], row[4]
        ll0 = length(row) >= 5 ? row[5] : NaN
        aic = -2*ll + 2*df
        bic = -2*ll + df*log(n)
        push!(aics, aic); push!(bics, bic)
        ll0_str = (ismissing(ll0) || !isfinite(ll0)) ?
                  "." : Printf.@sprintf("%.6g", ll0)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %10s %10s %10.7g %7d %10.7g %10.7g\n",
                       string(name), commafmt(n), ll0_str, ll, df, aic, bic)
    end
    println("-"^78)
    println("Note: BIC uses N = number of observations. See [R] IC note.")
    return (; aic = aics, bic = bics)
end

function poisson_stata(df, formula; vce::Symbol=:robust, level::Float64=0.95,
                       quiet::Bool=false,
                       layout::Union{Nothing,AbstractVector}=nothing,
                       header_style::Symbol=:poisson,
                       cluster_var=nothing)
    # Drop missing for variables in formula (and the cluster var, if any)
    needed = StatsModels.termvars(formula)
    cols   = cluster_var === nothing ? needed :
                                       vcat(needed, [Symbol(cluster_var)])
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, cols])
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing, Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(col)
        end
    end

    # Fit Poisson GLM
    m = GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink())
    β  = GLM.coef(m)
    cn = GLM.coefnames(m)
    n  = Int(StatsBase.nobs(m))
    yv = Float64.(GLM.response(m))
    μ  = GLM.predict(m)
    Xm = GLM.modelmatrix(m)
    k  = size(Xm, 2)

    # If `cluster_var` is given, force vce → :cluster regardless of caller's
    # choice (Stata's `vce(cluster <var>)` syntax), and capture cluster count.
    n_clusters = 0
    if cluster_var !== nothing
        vce = :cluster
        n_clusters = length(unique(dfc[!, Symbol(cluster_var)]))
    end

    # SE: robust sandwich (default) / cluster-robust (CR1) / OIM.
    # Stata's `vce(robust)` uses n/(n-1) finite-sample correction.
    # `vce(cluster G)` uses (G/(G-1))·(n-1)/(n-k) and aggregates scores by
    # cluster: B = Σ_g (X_g'(y_g − μ_g)) (X_g'(y_g − μ_g))'.
    if vce == :robust
        H = Xm' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(μ) * Xm
        meat = Xm' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal((yv .- μ).^2) * Xm
        Hinv = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.cholesky(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(H)))
        V = Hinv * meat * Hinv * (n / (n - 1))
    elseif vce == :cluster
        cluster_var === nothing &&
            error("vce = :cluster requires `cluster_var = :varname`")
        cl = dfc[!, Symbol(cluster_var)]
        u  = (yv .- μ) .* Xm                # n×k per-obs scores X_i·(y_i−μ_i)
        # Aggregate scores by cluster, then meat = Σ_g s_g s_g'.
        meat = zeros(k, k)
        for g in unique(cl)
            sg = vec(sum(u[cl .== g, :], dims = 1))
            meat .+= sg * sg'
        end
        H    = Xm' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(μ) * Xm
        Hinv = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.cholesky(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(H)))
        G    = n_clusters
        # Stata's `poisson, vce(cluster)` uses ONLY the G/(G−1) cluster
        # adjustment — no extra (n−1)/(n−k) factor (that one is OLS-style).
        V    = Hinv * meat * Hinv * (G / (G - 1))
    else
        V = Matrix(GLM.vcov(m))
    end
    se = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    z  = β ./ se
    p  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    ci_lo = β .- crit .* se
    ci_hi = β .+ crit .* se

    # Slopes (excluding intercept) — used for both Wald and LR
    intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx = setdiff(1:length(β), [intercept_idx])
    Wald = NaN; Wald_p = NaN
    if !isempty(slope_idx)
        β_slope = β[slope_idx]
        V_slope = V[slope_idx, slope_idx]
        Wald = β_slope' * LinearAlgebra.inv(V_slope) * β_slope
        Wald_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)), Wald)
    end

    # Log pseudolikelihood and Pseudo R² (McFadden's-like: 1 - LL/LL_null)
    ll  = GLM.loglikelihood(m)
    # Null model: intercept only
    m_null = GLM.glm(StatsModels.term(Symbol(formula.lhs)) ~ StatsModels.term(1),
                     dfc, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink())
    ll_null = GLM.loglikelihood(m_null)
    pseudo_r2 = 1 - ll / ll_null

    # LR chi² on slopes — Stata's default `poisson` reports `LR chi2(k)`;
    # `vce(robust|cluster)` switches it to `Wald chi2(k)` (LR is invalid
    # under misspecification of the likelihood).
    LR_chi2 = !isempty(slope_idx) ? 2 * (ll - ll_null) : NaN
    LR_p    = !isempty(slope_idx) ?
              1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)), LR_chi2) :
              NaN

    # Stata %9.0g formatter — sign-aware width cap (cap=9 except cap=10 for
    # negative |x|<1, where leading-zero strip saves a char). Without this
    # asymmetry, negative |x|<1 values would lose a digit vs Stata's output.
    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        if 0 < abs(x) < 1
            s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.")
        end
        return lpad(s, w)
    end
    function commafmt(num)
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1
            push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3
        end
        return (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    # Skip the entire Stata-style printout when quiet=true (mirrors Stata's
    # `quietly poisson ...`). Useful for chapter chunks that just need β/V/X
    # for downstream margins/dydx/etc. and don't want to repeat the table.
    if !quiet
    # Print Stata-style header. Two layouts:
    #   :poisson — Stata's `poisson` command output. Top-left says "Poisson
    #              regression", and the right column lists Number of obs /
    #              Wald chi2(k) / Prob > chi2 / Pseudo R2 over four lines,
    #              with "Log pseudolikelihood = …" on the last line at left.
    #   :ml      — Stata's `ml maximize` output. No "Poisson regression"
    #              header; the right column lists Number of obs / Wald
    #              chi2(k) / Prob > chi2 over three lines, with "Log
    #              [pseudo]likelihood = …" on the third line at left, and
    #              no Pseudo R2 row.
    println()
    if header_style == :ml
        # Stata `ml maximize` right-block format: 13-char left-padded label,
        # " = ", then a value field whose width is the max of the three
        # value strings plus 1 (so the longest value sits 1 space after `=`,
        # shorter ones are right-aligned). The whole right block is positioned
        # flush right at col 78 by adjusting the leading whitespace.
        nstr = commafmt(n)
        wstr = isfinite(Wald) ? Printf.@sprintf("%.2f", Wald) : ""
        pstr = isfinite(Wald) ? Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", Wald_p) : ""
        vw   = maximum(length, (nstr, wstr, pstr))
        rblock = 13 + 3 + vw
        lead   = max(0, 78 - rblock)
        ws     = " " ^ lead
        println(ws, rpad("Number of obs", 13), " = ", lpad(nstr, vw))
        if isfinite(Wald)
            println(ws, rpad("Wald chi2($(length(slope_idx)))", 13),
                    " = ", lpad(wstr, vw))
        end
        ll_label = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? "Log pseudolikelihood" : "Log likelihood"
        ll_str   = Printf.@sprintf("%s = %.3f", ll_label, ll)
        println(rpad(ll_str, lead), rpad("Prob > chi2", 13), " = ", lpad(pstr, vw))
    else
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %6s\n",
                       "Poisson regression", "Number of obs", commafmt(n))
        # `LR chi2` for OIM (default), `Wald chi2` for robust/cluster.
        chi2_label = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? "Wald" : "LR"
        chi2_val   = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? Wald   : LR_chi2
        chi2_p     = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? Wald_p : LR_p
        if isfinite(chi2_val)
            Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.2f\n", "",
                           "$chi2_label chi2($(length(slope_idx)))", chi2_val)
            Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.4f\n", "", "Prob > chi2", chi2_p)
        end
        ll_label = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ?
                   "Log pseudolikelihood" : "Log likelihood"
        ll_str = Printf.@sprintf("%s = %.5f", ll_label, ll)
        r2_str = Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %6.4f", "Pseudo R2", pseudo_r2)
        pad_h  = max(0, 78 - length(ll_str) - length(r2_str))
        println(ll_str, " "^pad_h, r2_str)
    end
    println()

    # Cluster sub-note (Stata: "(Std. err. adjusted for G clusters in <var>)"),
    # right-aligned at col 78.
    if vce == :cluster
        cl_str = Printf.@sprintf("(Std. err. adjusted for %d clusters in %s)",
                                 n_clusters, cluster_var)
        println(lpad(cl_str, 78))
    end

    # Coefficient table. Stata uses lowercase "std. err." under the "Robust"
    # subheader for `vce(robust)` / `vce(cluster …)` and capital "Std. err."
    # for the default OIM.
    println("-"^78)
    if vce == :robust || vce == :cluster
        println("             |               Robust")
    end
    se_label = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? "std. err." : "Std. err."
    Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  %s      z    P>|z|     [95%% conf. interval]\n",
                   string(formula.lhs), se_label)
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)

    # `_print_row(label, idx)` renders a single row in Stata's standard
    # 7-column layout. `_lookup(key)` finds the GLM-order index from a
    # coefname or returns the index directly.
    _print_row(label, idx) = Printf.@printf(
        "%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
        label, g9(β[idx]; w=10), g9(se[idx]; w=9),
        Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z[idx]),
        Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p[idx]),
        g9(ci_lo[idx]; w=9), g9(ci_hi[idx]; w=10))
    _lookup(key) = key isa Integer ? Int(key) :
        (let i = findfirst(==(string(key)), cn)
            i === nothing && error("'$(key)' not found in coefnames=$(cn)")
            i
        end)

    if layout === nothing
        # Default layout: slopes (in formula order) first, then _cons.
        for i in slope_idx
            _print_row(cn[i], i)
        end
        intercept_idx !== nothing && _print_row("_cons", intercept_idx)
    else
        # Custom layout. Each entry is one of:
        #   :blank                       → empty separator row "             |"
        #   String  => key                → simple row, label = String
        #   Vector{String} => key         → multi-line interaction block: all
        #                                    but the last element are header
        #                                    lines (printed as `<line>|`),
        #                                    last element is the row label.
        # `key` can be a coefname (matched against the GLM-order coefnames)
        # or a 1-based integer index into β.
        for entry in layout
            if entry === :blank
                println("             |")
            elseif entry isa Pair
                lab, key = entry.first, entry.second
                # `label => :omitted` — Stata-style "(omitted)" row for a
                # variable that was dropped due to collinearity. Prints
                # "        label |          0  (omitted)" with no key lookup.
                if key === :omitted
                    Printf.@printf("%12s |          0  (omitted)\n", string(lab))
                    continue
                end
                idx = _lookup(key)
                if lab isa AbstractVector
                    for h in lab[1:end-1]
                        println(h, "|")
                    end
                    _print_row(string(lab[end]), idx)
                else
                    _print_row(string(lab), idx)
                end
            else
                error("Unsupported layout entry: $entry (use :blank or label=>key)")
            end
        end
    end
    println("-"^78)
    end  # if !quiet

    # Return values in *Stata's display order*: slopes first, then _cons.
    # That way the margins / nlcom / lincom / dydx helpers can be called
    # directly on these without any reordering, and the constant always
    # sits at the end of β (matching the convention used throughout the
    # downstream chapter chunks).
    if intercept_idx === nothing
        ord = collect(slope_idx)
        cn_ord = cn[ord]
    else
        ord = vcat(collect(slope_idx), [intercept_idx])
        cn_ord = vcat(cn[slope_idx], "_cons")
    end
    β_ord  = β[ord]
    se_ord = se[ord]
    V_ord  = V[ord, ord]
    X_ord  = Xm[:, ord]   # last column = ones (the constant)

    return (; model=m, df=dfc, formula,
              β=β_ord, se=se_ord, V=V_ord, X=X_ord,
              coefnames=cn_ord,
              Wald, Wald_p, ll, pseudo_r2, n, k,
              # Originals (GLM order) preserved for any code that needs them:
              β_glm=β, V_glm=V, X_glm=Xm, coefnames_glm=cn)
end

"""
    probit_stata(df, formula; vce=:oim, level=0.95, quiet=false) -> NamedTuple

Stata-style `probit <depvar> <regs> [, vce(robust)]`. Fits a Binomial GLM
with `ProbitLink` and prints Stata's exact `probit` output:

  - Header: Number of obs / LR chi2(k) / Prob > chi2 / Log likelihood / Pseudo R²
```
